First, let's define the sets:
- \( S \) is the set of squares.
- \( C \) is the set of cubes.
- \( F \) is the set of perfect fifth powers.

We want to count the number of integers from 1 to \( n \) that are in at least one of these sets. Let \( |S| \) be the number of squares, \( |C| \) be the number of cubes, and \( |F| \) be the number of perfect fifth powers. The number of integers from 1 to \( n \) that are in at least one of these sets is given by:
\[ |S \cup C \cup F| = |S| + |C| + |F| - |S \cap C| - |S \cap F| - |C \cap F| + |S \cap C \cap F|. \]

The number of integers from 1 to \( n \) that are not in any of these sets is:
\[ n - |S \cup C \cup F|. \]

We need to calculate the number of integers up to \( n \) that are squares, cubes, or perfect fifth powers. The number of squares up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor \), the number of cubes up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[3]{n} \rfloor \), and the number of perfect fifth powers up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[5]{n} \rfloor \).

The number of integers that are both squares and cubes (i.e., sixth powers) up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[6]{n} \rfloor \), the number of integers that are both squares and fifth powers (i.e., tenth powers) up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[10]{n} \rfloor \), and the number of integers that are both cubes and fifth powers (i.e., fifteenth powers) up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[15]{n} \rfloor \).

The number of integers that are squares, cubes, and fifth powers (i.e., thirtieth powers) up to \( n \) is \( \lfloor \sqrt[30]{n} \rfloor \).

Thus, we have:
\[ |S \cup C \cup F| = \lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[3]{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[5]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[6]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[10]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[15]{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[30]{n} \rfloor. \]

We need to find the smallest \( n \) such that:
\[ n - \left( \lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[3]{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[5]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[6]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[10]{n} \rfloor - \lfloor \sqrt[15]{n} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt[30]{n} \rfloor \right) \geq 1000. \]
